analysis.title: Federal Reserve preview: A pause before a December hike
key_insights: ING expects the Fed to hold rates at the 28 October FOMC meeting, in line with markets and economists, despite hot September inflation prints.

The September core CPI print was 0.3% month-on-month and briefly pushed the chance of an October hike above 50%. Comments from Vice Chairs Jefferson and Bowman and Governor Waller signalling no rush quickly calmed markets.
Chair Warsh did not talk up the chances of action at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, unlike at Jackson Hole before the September hike, which further reduced the perceived odds of an October move.

The decision is unlikely to be unanimous. Four FOMC members projected 50bp of hikes by year-end in the latest Summary of Economic Projections, and Hammack, Kashkari and Logan voted to hike in July and could dissent for a hike again.

ING expects a brief press release and a short, matter-of-fact press conference from Warsh, who is not keen on forward guidance. The message is likely that the economy is in decent shape, unemployment is low, inflation is above target and policy will follow incoming data.

ING forecasts a 25bp hike in December, leaving the Fed funds target range at 4-4.25%, followed by a pause through December 2027, when the December 2026 hike is reversed. This matches consensus. The Fed's own projections show one hike this year and no change in 2027.

ING's path assumes that in the months after the midterm elections an agreement improves energy flows from the Persian Gulf and sharply cuts shipping and insurance costs. That would lower pump prices and let inflation fall back to 2% in 2H 2027.
The risk to ING's view is a longer-lasting conflict. ING would not rule out additional hikes in 1Q 2027, but a weaker economy would then bring faster and larger cuts in 2H 2027 than in the base case.

A strong Treasury performance last week eased the prior tightening impulse. The 10yr yield is below 5% after an earlier break above 5.25%. ING doubts the decline will persist and expects the yield to move back above 5% on inflation, fiscal deficit and AI-boom pressures.
Risk-off conditions and the sell-off in French bonds make this a poor meeting for the Fed to tighten. ING sees it as the right meeting to hold.
The Fed is unlikely to set out a balance sheet reduction plan soon. Committee recommendations are expected closer to the turn of the year, and repo markets are behaving better than a year ago.

The dollar should keep most of its September gains because Fed communication is likely to support higher US yields. A renewed tech-led risk-off move, not dovish Fed messaging, is the more likely trigger for a dollar correction.

The dollar rose about 4% through September and early October and is now consolidating. Rate differentials moved slightly against it this month as the US tech sell-off pared back Fed tightening expectations.
Warsh-led FOMC meetings have set the four-to-six-week dollar trend this year: June was hawkish, July was seen as dovish and September was a hawkish hike.

ING expects Warsh to avoid concluding that wider credit spreads and softer equities mean fewer hikes are needed, after criticism of his July remarks that the bond market was doing the tightening. ING expects EUR/USD to fall back to the year's lows near 1.11 on higher energy prices and French political risk.

sector_views.rationale: Interest rate-sensitive sectors such as housing are experiencing increasing pain, and housing disinflation is expected to help bring inflation down.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A surprise to the upside that briefly pushed October hike odds above 50% before Fed comments calmed markets.
ING expects a December hike followed by a pause through December 2027, when the hike is reversed.
Markets, economists and ING all expect no change, with possible hawkish dissents.
The yield fell below 5% after an earlier break above 5.25%. ING expects it to move back above 5%.
Benign wage growth supports ING's view that inflation can fall back to 2% in 2H 2027.
Depends on an energy deal that cuts shipping and insurance costs and on more housing disinflation.
ING expects a return to the lows of the year near 1.11.

risk_factors: A longer-lasting Persian Gulf conflict would keep energy prices and inflation higher and could bring additional hikes in 1Q 2027.
Higher bond yields could push mortgage rates and corporate borrowing costs to new cycle highs and weaken the economy.
The November CPI is released the day after the Fed meeting and officials will probably see it before the December decision, so a surprise cannot be ruled out.
French bond market stress adds to systemic pressure.
A renewed tech-led risk-off move could push the dollar lower.
vol_and_positioning: Rate differentials have moved slightly against the dollar this month because the US tech sell-off pared back Fed tightening expectations.
The dollar rose about 4% through September and early October and has entered a consolidative phase.
geopolitical: Persian Gulf conflict affecting energy flows, shipping costs and insurance costs, with ING assuming an agreement in the couple of months after the US midterm elections
French political risk and a sell-off in French bonds adding to broader bond market stress

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: inflation is above target, the economy is growing robustly and four FOMC members projected 50bp of hikes by year-end, so Hammack, Kashkari and Logan could dissent for a hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: recent jobs numbers have disappointed, housing is under pressure, officials signalled no rush, and risk-off conditions and bond market stress make this the wrong meeting to tighten.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A surprise in the November CPI, released the day after the Fed meeting, could change the December call.

theme_stances.key_argument: Ongoing concerns about elevated price pressures mean ING expects a December interest rate rise after an October hold.
theme_stances.evidence: This is in line with the current consensus forecast
